paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's people sing because God rescued them, and then God asks them to LISTEN. This psalm opens with tambourines and harps, but the heart of it is God saying, "O Israel, if only you would listen to Me!" (Psalm 81:8). He had relieved their shoulders, answered them in distress, and brought them up out of Egypt (Psalm 81:6, 7, 10). A song without listening is just noise, and I know noise, because I have a whole bakery full of ovens that never clap back.

Now the hard part. God says, "But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me." (Psalm 81:11). So He gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices (Psalm 81:12). Oof. I think that line is heavy, and it's a good reminder that ignoring God's voice is never a small thing. But look at what comes right after: God says it again, "If only My people would listen to Me, if Israel would follow My ways" (Psalm 81:13). I think that sounds like a God who still wants to be heard.

And that's the good news, baker. God doesn't just want obedience, He wants to give. He said, "Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it." (Psalm 81:10), and He closes the psalm with the finest wheat and "honey from the rock" (Psalm 81:16). So the question for you today is simple: are you listening for His voice in His Word? That's how I plan to stay ready in my bakery, with my ears open and my mouth WIDE open, because He's the one doing the filling.
